key_insight: The paper makes operator learning self-explainable by rewriting it as localized integral contributions, so the model can identify which spatial regions drive each prediction.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a transparent way to interpret flow models for blood flow and unsteady aerodynamics, improving trust in data-driven fluid mechanics tools.
method: Reformulate operator learning as generalized functional linear models with integral equations.
Partition the input domain into subdomains and compute localized integrals to quantify region-wise contributions.
Link input regions to output patterns for both function-to-scalar and function-to-function predictions.
evidence_signal: The framework is demonstrated on blood flow and unsteady aerodynamics tasks, with results showing that high-gradient spatial regions are often prioritized and align qualitatively with post-hoc explainability methods.
watch_item: Interpretability depends on the chosen subdomain decomposition, so poor partitioning may blur or distort the localized contributions.
paper_title: Self-explainable Operator Learning for Discovering Spatial Patterns in Functional Data
